name: Hadad
overview: Hadad the Edomite is a male figure identified in Scripture by his unique attribute as an Edomite, mentioned specifically in 1 Kings 11:14. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him. His role is noted within the context of Edom, a neighboring nation to Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Hadad means 'thunderer,' which is a proper name not given by God, as recorded in 1 Kings 11:14. This name reflects a powerful natural phenomenon, though the text does not elaborate further on the significance of the name in his life or role.
familyAndRelationships: Hadad is inferred to be the son of Genubath, according to 1 Kings 11:20. Additionally, he is suggested to have a brother-in-law relationship with Pharaoh, as inferred from 1 Kings 1:19. Beyond these connections, Scripture does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Hadad the Edomite appears in the biblical narrative as a notable adversary during the reign of Solomon, reflecting the ongoing tensions between Israel and Edom. His identification as an Edomite and his familial ties to Egypt through Pharaoh highlight the geopolitical alliances and conflicts of the time. Though not extensively detailed, his presence underscores God's sovereign control over nations surrounding Israel and the unfolding of His purposes in history.
